sections.title: AI Mode — documents first, fewer questions
sections.intro: Upload the same papers a CPA would ask for (1040, W-2, statements). Local AI and parsers extract your income, taxes, and more. You only answer what documents can't provide. Market assumptions can still use AI Estimates later.

where_to_get.p: Personal PDFs are parsed on this Mac with local Ollama (when available). Nothing from those files is uploaded for extraction.
After documents, Estimates helps with non-personal assumptions (inflation, returns, some healthcare defaults)—not for reading your tax PDFs.

sections.title: Link your bank & investment accounts
sections.intro: The fastest way to fill in balances is a secure read-only connection. Same login you use on Chase.com, Fidelity.com, etc. — we never see your password.

where_to_get.p: Use the same username and password as your bank or brokerage website or mobile app.
Current checking, savings, credit card, and investment balances — used for starting assets in your plan.
Skip this step and upload brokerage or 401(k) statements in a later step instead.

sections.title: Your tax return (income + taxes)
sections.intro: Upload your most recent Form 1040. It fills in wages (line 1z), filing status, deductions, state, pension, rental income, and more — one document for income and taxes.

where_to_get.p: Open last year's return and export or print to PDF — include all pages if you itemize (Schedule A, Schedule E).
Ask for a PDF copy of the filed return (all schedules).
You'll review each field before it's applied, then see a summary of what was imported so you can confirm it looks right.

sections.title: How much you spend each year
sections.intro: Refresh expenses from Plaid (cards + checking), then open the Spending builder to break retirement costs into categories — rent, mortgage, food, healthcare, and more. We’ll pre-fill what we can. Upload a mortgage statement or Form 1098 for payment and payoff year (1040 only has interest for taxes).

where_to_get.p: Click Refresh expenses — we annualize card and checking history. Credit cards count as spending (not assets).

Upload a recent lender statement (balance, monthly payment, interest rate). We compute maturity year from those and keep the payment in expenses until that year — including after you retire — then living costs drop by the mortgage amount. Form 1098 covers deducted interest for taxes.
Upload each county/city tax bill (multiple properties OK — we sum them). This is cash-flow spending. Your 1040 Schedule A SALT is separate for tax modeling and may be capped.
Open Spending builder to enter or adjust categories. Mortgage is tracked separately until payoff year; everything else rolls into Base Expenses.
Skip refresh and use Spending builder (or Guided) to enter categories manually.

sections.title: 401(k), IRA & brokerage statements
sections.intro: Optional but helpful — confirms retirement account balances Plaid might not fully capture.

where_to_get.p: Latest quarterly statement from Fidelity NetBenefits, Vanguard, Empower, etc. — PDF from the provider website.
Most recent statement from the custodian (Fidelity, Schwab, Vanguard).
Monthly or quarterly statement showing total account value.

sections.title: Social Security statement
sections.intro: Add file(s) → Extract → Apply. We read the monthly benefit chart (or SSA-1099) and fill your plan’s SS fields. Tag You or Spouse on a joint plan.

where_to_get.p: ssa.gov → my Social Security → download your statement PDF. Prefer the official digital PDF (not a photo of a printout).
SS benefit mode (PIA), monthly amount at full retirement age, annual SS amount (monthly × 12), and SS start age (usually FRA).
If you already receive benefits, the January SSA-1099 works too (net benefits paid).
Upload each spouse’s statement separately and tag Spouse on the second file before Extract.

sections.title: Inflation & investment returns
sections.intro: No documents needed — we refresh public market data for planning assumptions.

where_to_get.p: Click Refresh market to pull current inflation and return assumptions from FRED and market data.

sections.title: Anything documents couldn't answer
sections.intro: Retirement age, life expectancy, and some healthcare choices usually aren't on tax forms. Enter them in Guided, or continue and use AI Estimates for non-personal assumptions.

where_to_get.p: Open Guided for remaining personal facts (age targets, healthcare choices).
On the next step / Guided AI screen: fill inflation, returns, and other defaults that aren't on your 1040.

sections.title: AI Estimates (non-personal assumptions)
sections.intro: Optional: fill market and healthcare defaults that aren't on your tax documents. This uses your configured estimate provider (settings) — not for parsing personal PDFs. Personal docs stay local-only on upload steps.

where_to_get.p: Inflation, investment returns, and similar assumptions. User income/assets should already come from documents above.

sections.title: Review what you've provided
sections.intro: Summary of documents and plan completeness. Switch to Guided to fine-tune gaps, or run your plan when ready.
